docs.title: nyx-bridge-maya
docs.text:
Connects Autodesk Maya to a running Nyx, so stages can send commands to Maya and get the results back. It is the Maya client of nyx-bridge: Maya connects out to the bridge server of Nyx, Nyx never launches or reaches into Maya on its own.

# in Maya's Script Editor
import maya.cmds as cmds

cmds.loadPlugin("nyx_bridge_maya_plugin")
cmds.nyxBridge(start=True)        # connects, retrying until Nyx is up

# in mayapy
import nyx_bridge_maya

nyx_bridge_maya.MayaClient().serve_forever()
If you want to... Read Install the module and connect Maya to Nyx User Guide Work on nyx-bridge-maya, run its tests in mayapy Developer Guide Look up a class or function API reference (see the navigation)

Requires Maya 2026 (Python 3.11) or any Maya whose Python is 3.11 to 3.13. See also nyx-bridge-blender.

docs.title: MayaClient
docs.text:
Bases: NyxClient

Nyx client living in Maya.

What Nyx sends is run on Maya's main thread, so it can use maya.cmds safely. Scripts find cmds, mel and om (maya.api.OpenMaya) in their namespace.

Serve from a background thread (start_in_thread, what start does) in an interactive Maya. In mayapy serve from the main thread with serve_forever, there is no event loop to hand work over to.

def run_on_main_thread(self, func: typing.Callable[[], typing.Any]) -> typing.Any:
    """Run a function on Maya's main thread and wait for its result.

    Args:
        func (Callable[[], Any]): function to run.

    Returns:
        Any: whatever the function returns.
    """
    if threading.current_thread() is threading.main_thread():
        return func()

    import maya.utils

    return maya.utils.executeInMainThreadWithResult(func)

docs.title: serve_standalone(name=None, address=None, token=None, connect_timeout=None)
docs.text:
Serve Nyx from the main thread of a Maya without a UI, until Nyx is done with it.

For mayapy, after maya.standalone.initialize: there is no event loop to hand work to, so the requests run right on the calling thread. Returns when Nyx asks the client to shut down or the connection ends, it does not reconnect. Start it from a Launch Process node of Nyx with a command like

"$MAYAPY" -c "import maya.standalone; maya.standalone.initialize(name='python');
import nyx_bridge_maya; nyx_bridge_maya.serve_standalone();
maya.standalone.uninitialize()"

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default name str | None

name Nyx shows for this Maya, NYX_BRIDGE_CLIENT_NAME if omitted, then derived from the process id.

None address str | tuple[str, int] | None

host:port of Nyx, see start.

None token str | None

token of the Nyx server.

None connect_timeout float | None

seconds to keep trying to reach Nyx, forever if omitted.

None Source code in src/nyx_bridge_maya/client.py 
def serve_standalone(
    name: str | None = None,
    address: str | tuple[str, int] | None = None,
    token: str | None = None,
    connect_timeout: float | None = None,
) -> None:
    """Serve Nyx from the main thread of a Maya without a UI, until Nyx is done with it.

    For `mayapy`, after `maya.standalone.initialize`: there is no event loop to hand
    work to, so the requests run right on the calling thread. Returns when Nyx asks the
    client to shut down or the connection ends, it does not reconnect. Start it from a
    Launch Process node of Nyx with a command like

        "$MAYAPY" -c "import maya.standalone; maya.standalone.initialize(name='python');
        import nyx_bridge_maya; nyx_bridge_maya.serve_standalone();
        maya.standalone.uninitialize()"

    Args:
        name (str | None): name Nyx shows for this Maya, `NYX_BRIDGE_CLIENT_NAME` if
            omitted, then derived from the process id.
        address (str | tuple[str, int] | None): `host:port` of Nyx, see `start`.
        token (str | None): token of the Nyx server.
        connect_timeout (float | None): seconds to keep trying to reach Nyx, forever if
            omitted.
    """
    MayaClient(
        name=name or os.environ.get(CLIENT_NAME_VARIABLE) or None,
        address=address,
        token=token,
        reconnect=False,
    ).serve_forever(connect_timeout)

docs.title: start(address=None, token=None, name=None)
docs.text:
Connect Maya to Nyx from a background thread, and keep trying until it works.

Where Nyx is comes from the arguments, then the environment, then the address file Nyx writes, see nyx_bridge.protocol.find_server_address. It does not matter whether Nyx is already running: the client connects once it is, and again if the connection drops.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default address str | tuple[str, int] | None

host:port of Nyx.

None token str | None

token of the Nyx server.

None name str | None

name Nyx shows for this Maya. Derived from the process id if omitted.

None

Returns:

Name Type Description MayaClient MayaClient

the running client. An already running one is returned as it is, the arguments are ignored.

Source code in src/nyx_bridge_maya/client.py 
def start(
    address: str | tuple[str, int] | None = None,
    token: str | None = None,
    name: str | None = None,
) -> MayaClient:
    """Connect Maya to Nyx from a background thread, and keep trying until it works.

    Where Nyx is comes from the arguments, then the environment, then the address file
    Nyx writes, see `nyx_bridge.protocol.find_server_address`. It does not matter
    whether Nyx is already running: the client connects once it is, and again if
    the connection drops.

    Args:
        address (str | tuple[str, int] | None): `host:port` of Nyx.
        token (str | None): token of the Nyx server.
        name (str | None): name Nyx shows for this Maya. Derived from the process id
            if omitted.

    Returns:
        MayaClient: the running client. An already running one is returned as it is,
            the arguments are ignored.
    """
    global _client, _thread
    if is_running():
        return _client
    _client = MayaClient(name=name, address=address, token=token)
    _thread = _client.start_in_thread()
    return _client

docs.title: stop()
docs.text:
Disconnect from Nyx and stop the client started by start.

Source code in src/nyx_bridge_maya/client.py 
def stop() -> None:
    """Disconnect from Nyx and stop the client started by `start`."""
    global _client, _thread
    client, thread = _client, _thread
    _client = _thread = None
    if client is not None:
        client.stop()
    if thread is not None and thread is not threading.current_thread():
        thread.join(timeout=5)

docs.title: NyxBridgeCommand
docs.text:
Bases: MPxCommand

Connect Maya to Nyx, disconnect it, or ask about the connection.

Python

cmds.nyxBridge(start=True) cmds.nyxBridge(start=True, address="127.0.0.1:47770", token="...", name="rig") cmds.nyxBridge(query=True, connected=True) # [True] once Nyx accepted Maya cmds.nyxBridge(query=True, running=True) cmds.nyxBridge(stop=True)

Maya hands back the result of a Python command as a list, nyx_bridge_maya. is_connected() and is_running() answer with a plain bool.

docs.title: create_syntax() staticmethod
docs.text:
Create the syntax of the command, for Maya.

Source code in src/nyx_bridge_maya/command.py 
@staticmethod
def create_syntax() -> om.MSyntax:
    """Create the syntax of the command, for Maya."""
    syntax = om.MSyntax()
    syntax.enableQuery = True
    for flag in (START_FLAG, STOP_FLAG, RUNNING_FLAG, CONNECTED_FLAG):
        syntax.addFlag(*flag)
    for flag in (ADDRESS_FLAG, TOKEN_FLAG, NAME_FLAG):
        syntax.addFlag(*flag, om.MSyntax.kString)
    return syntax

docs.title: doIt(args)
docs.text:
Answer the query, or do what the flags say. Stopping goes before starting, so using both restarts the client.

Source code in src/nyx_bridge_maya/command.py 
def doIt(self, args) -> None:
    """Answer the query, or do what the flags say. Stopping goes before starting,
    so using both restarts the client."""
    parser = om.MArgParser(self.syntax(), args)
    if parser.isQuery:
        self._answer_query(parser)
        return

    if parser.isFlagSet(STOP_FLAG[0]):
        client.stop()
    if parser.isFlagSet(START_FLAG[0]):
        client.start(
            address=self._string_flag(parser, ADDRESS_FLAG),
            token=self._string_flag(parser, TOKEN_FLAG),
            name=self._string_flag(parser, NAME_FLAG),
        )

docs.title: Developer Guide
docs.text: This guide is for people who work on nyx-bridge-maya itself.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
uv sync
make check        # ruff + pytest in mayapy
make mkdocs       # serve these docs

make help lists every target. Ruff uses a line length of 89 and the E, F and UP rules. Docstrings are Google style: the API reference is generated from them.

Tests need a Maya: see Testing for the .env file and how they run.

Important

import nyx_bridge_maya must work outside Maya (docs, tooling), so maya.* modules are imported inside the methods that use them. Only command.py and the plug-in import maya.api.OpenMaya at the top, since Maya is the only one loading them.

Member Maya specific CLIENT_KIND "maya" client_version() cmds.about(version=True) default_namespace() cmds, mel, om (maya.api.OpenMaya) run_on_main_thread(func) Runs func directly on the main thread, else maya.utils.executeInMainThreadWithResult.

docs.title: Two ways to serve
docs.text:
• Interactive Maya: start() uses start_in_thread(). The reading loop lives on a daemon thread, and every execution is handed to Maya's main thread through executeInMainThreadWithResult, which needs Maya's event loop.
  • mayapy: there is no event loop, so handing work over would wait forever. serve_standalone() serves from the main thread with serve_forever(), where run_on_main_thread calls func straight away. reconnect=False, since the process is started for one stage.

docs.title: Module state
docs.text: client.py keeps one client and its thread in module globals. start() returns the running one, stop() clears them and joins the thread (5 s). The plug-in's uninitializePlugin calls stop(), so unloading never leaves a connection behind.

docs.title: The command
docs.text: NyxBridgeCommand (command.py) is a thin layer over those functions, written for the Python API 2.0 (maya_useNewAPI in the plug-in). -stop is handled before -start, so both together restart the client. Queries use setResult, which Maya returns as a list.

docs.title: The module
docs.text:
make dist installs the package from the project folder into dist/nyx_bridge_maya_module/python (so dependencies that are git sources in [tool.uv.sources] resolve) and copies src/plug-ins next to it. The .mod template has @VERSION@ and @MODULE_ROOT@ filled in by sed. The targets come from sowwic/makefiles (dcc/maya), fetched into .make/ and committed; make update-make fetches them again.

DIST_EXTRAS (space or comma separated, empty by default) installs optional dependencies of the package into the module as well: make dist DIST_EXTRAS=usd runs uv pip install --target ... ".[usd]". The extras are declared in [project.optional-dependencies] of pyproject.toml; today there is usd (sowwic-nyx-usd).

docs.title: Branches and versions
docs.text:
develop is the default and PR branch; main is the release branch. Work on a feature branch named after the GitHub issue (3-update-nyx-bridge-dependency).

The version lives in VERSION. make update-version copies it into pyproject.toml. Add a v<version> section at the top of CHANGELOG.rst, one bullet per user-visible change with the issue number where there is one.

nyx-bridge-maya depends on sowwic-nyx-bridge. When a new nyx-bridge release is needed, raise the minimum in pyproject.toml, run uv lock and add a changelog bullet.

docs.title: Release
docs.text:
1. Update CHANGELOG.rst and VERSION (make update-version), commit on main.
  2. Run
make release VERSION=1.2.3 [RELEASE_TITLE="..."]

It tags main, pushes and merges back into develop. The tag triggers .github/workflows/release.yml, which creates the GitHub release from the changelog section.

docs.title: CI
docs.text: Workflows in .github/workflows/ are thin callers of the shared ones in sowwic/gh-workflows: tests (on a self-hosted Maya runner, see Testing), lint, docs deployment to GitHub Pages and the release. Dependabot opens update PRs against develop.

docs.title: Testing
docs.text:
The tests need Maya's modules, so they run inside mayapy with maya.standalone.

make pytest                                  # everything, with coverage
./mayapy_test.sh -k plugin                   # extra arguments go to pytest
make pytest-pdb                              # verbose, pdb on failure

Do not pass the tests folder or a path to mayapy_test.sh: the script always runs tests/ itself, and a second spelling of the same path makes pytest refuse its conftest.py twice. Select tests with -k instead, e.g. ./mayapy_test.sh -k test_client.

docs.title: Setting up
docs.text:
1. Install Maya (2026 matches the project's python_version).
  2. Create .env in the project root (git-ignored), or ~/.config/maya-ci.env, or point MAYA_CI_ENV_FILE at a file:
MAYAPY=/Applications/Autodesk/maya2026/Maya.app/Contents/bin/mayapy
MAYA_MODULE_PATH=~/Library/Preferences/Autodesk/maya/modules
  1. Make the virtualenv use the same Python as Maya, so linting and editor tooling agree with what the tests run on:
make venv      # rewrites .python-version from MAYAPY and recreates .venv
uv sync

docs.title: What mayapy_test.sh does
docs.text:
1. Reads the env file and requires MAYAPY.
  2. Builds a temporary Maya module in build/maya_pytest/: installs the package and the maya-pytest dependency group (pytest, pytest-cov, pytest-mock) into python/, copies src/plug-ins, writes a .mod file.
  3. Puts that folder on MAYA_MODULE_PATH and clears PYTHONPATH, so the tests import the installed package, the same layout Maya loads, not src/.
  4. Starts mayapy, initializes maya.standalone, runs pytest.main and uninitializes.

Because the package is installed fresh each run, a change in src/ is picked up without any extra step. A missing test dependency goes into the maya-pytest group of pyproject.toml, not dev.

docs.title: Layout
docs.text:
File Covers tests/test_package.py The package imports. tests/test_client.py MayaClient against a real BridgeServer over loopback: description, namespace, errors, serve_standalone. tests/test_plugin.py Loading the plug-in, the nyxBridge flags, start/stop, unloading disconnecting.

tests/conftest.py initializes maya.standalone once per session (autouse) and provides output_dir.

docs.title: Fixtures and helpers
docs.text:
• server (BridgeServer(port=0)): the system picks a free port, so tests can run while Nyx is open.
  • make_client(server, **kwargs): a MayaClient pointed at that server with reconnect=False.
  • run_remote(server, client, *requests) (test_client.py): the client serves on the main thread, as in mayapy, while another thread sends the requests and collects results.
  • wait_until(predicate, timeout=15) (test_plugin.py): poll instead of sleep.

docs.title: What to cover
docs.text:
• A new nyxBridge flag: a test in test_plugin.py that loads the plug-in and goes through cmds.nyxBridge.
  • Anything that depends on threads: keep timeouts generous (15 s) and wait on conditions. A flaky test here is almost always a missing wait.
  • A hook that needs Maya's event loop (executeInMainThreadWithResult) can't be exercised in mayapy; test it with a mock (pytest-mock) of maya.utils.
  • Check in an interactive Maya when a change touches the main-thread hand-off.

docs.title: CI
docs.text:
.github/workflows/unit_tests.yml calls the shared maya-tests workflow on a self-hosted runner with Maya installed; GitHub's hosted runners have no Maya. Its .env lives on the runner. Run it on the current branch with:

make dispatch-pytest        # needs the gh CLI

Lint (code_quality.yml) runs on hosted runners and doesn't need Maya: make lint.

docs.title: User Guide
docs.text: This guide is for people who connect Maya to Nyx.

docs.title: Pages
docs.text: Page What you learn Installation Installing the Maya module, the .mod file, checking that Maya finds it. Connecting Maya to Nyx The nyxBridge command, the Python API, addresses and tokens, what scripts see. Starting Maya from a stage Headless mayapy started by a Launch Process node.

docs.title: How it fits together
docs.text:
Nyx                                       Maya
┌──────────────┐   Maya connects out    ┌───────────────────┐
│ BridgeServer │ ◀───────────────────── │ MayaClient        │
│              │ ───── execute ───────▶ │ runs on the main  │
│ ClientSession│ ◀──── result ───────── │ thread            │
└──────────────┘                        └───────────────────┘
  1. Nyx listens on a local port and holds a secret token.
  2. Maya starts a MayaClient (with the nyxBridge command or nyx_bridge_maya.start()), which keeps trying until Nyx accepts it.
  3. Nyx sends code; Maya runs it on its main thread and answers with the value and the captured output.

Protocol and server details are in the nyx-bridge documentation.

docs.title: Connecting Maya to Nyx
docs.text: Once the module is installed, Maya connects to Nyx in one of three ways. All of them start a MayaClient, which keeps retrying until Nyx is running, and connects again if the connection drops.

docs.title: The nyxBridge command
docs.text:
Provided by the plug-in:

import maya.cmds as cmds

cmds.loadPlugin("nyx_bridge_maya_plugin")
cmds.nyxBridge(start=True)                      # connect, retrying until Nyx is up
cmds.nyxBridge(query=True, connected=True)      # [True] once Nyx accepted Maya
cmds.nyxBridge(query=True, running=True)        # [True] while the client is serving
cmds.nyxBridge(stop=True)
Flag Short Meaning -start -s Start the client. Does nothing if one is already running. -stop -x Disconnect and stop it. Used together with -start it restarts. -running -r Query: the client is serving, connected or not. -connected -c Query: Nyx has accepted Maya. -address -a host:port of Nyx. -token -t Token of the Nyx server. -name -n Name Nyx shows for this Maya.

Maya hands back the result of a Python command as a list, so a query gives [True]. Unloading the plug-in disconnects.

docs.title: From Python
docs.text:
Without the plug-in:

import nyx_bridge_maya

nyx_bridge_maya.start()                         # background thread, returns the client
nyx_bridge_maya.is_running()
nyx_bridge_maya.is_connected()                  # plain bool
nyx_bridge_maya.stop()

start(address=None, token=None, name=None) returns the already running client if there is one and ignores its arguments then.

docs.title: Finding Nyx
docs.text:
Maya looks for the host, port and token in this order:

  1. The address and token arguments (-address and -token of the command).
  2. The environment: NYX_BRIDGE_ADDRESS (host:port) with NYX_BRIDGE_TOKEN.
  3. The address file a running Nyx writes.

On the same machine nothing needs to be configured. For Nyx on another machine pass address="host:port" and token=.... Details are in Finding the server.

docs.title: What scripts see
docs.text:
What Nyx sends runs on Maya's main thread, so maya.cmds is safe to use. The namespace of a connection lives as long as the connection, and starts with:

Name Is cmds maya.cmds mel maya.mel om maya.api.OpenMaya 
# what a stage sends
result = cmds.polyCube(name="box")[0]

Printed output is sent back, an exception comes back as an error of that execution and Maya keeps working. Executions run one at a time: while a long script runs, Maya's UI is busy as with any script run in the Script Editor.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text: Connections are logged to nyx_bridge_maya.client (and nyx_bridge.client) at INFO.

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: nyx-bridge-maya is installed as a Maya module: a folder with the Python package and the plug-in, found through a .mod file in Maya's module path. The package and its dependency (sowwic-nyx-bridge) live in the module, so nothing is installed into Maya's own Python.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
• Maya 2026 or another Maya with Python 3.11 to 3.13.
  • uv and make, to build the module from source.

docs.title: 1. Tell the build where Maya is
docs.text:
Create a .env file in the project root (or ~/.config/maya-ci.env):

MAYAPY=/Applications/Autodesk/maya2026/Maya.app/Contents/bin/mayapy
MAYA_MODULE_PATH=~/Library/Preferences/Autodesk/maya/modules
Variable Meaning MAYAPY The mayapy of the Maya you use. Only needed for tests and make venv. MAYA_MODULE_PATH Folder the .mod file is copied to. With several folders separated by : the first one is used.

Typical module folders:

Platform Folder macOS ~/Library/Preferences/Autodesk/maya/modules Windows %USERPROFILE%\Documents\maya\modules Linux ~/maya/modules

The file is looked up in this order: MAYA_CI_ENV_FILE, ./.env, ~/.config/maya-ci.env.

docs.title: 2. Install
docs.text:
make install

This runs two steps you can also run alone:

Target What it does make dist Assembles dist/nyx_bridge_maya_module/ with python/ (the package and its dependencies) and plug-ins/. make install-module Writes dist/nyx_bridge_maya.mod from templates/nyx_bridge_maya.mod and copies it to MAYA_MODULE_PATH.

The installed .mod file points at the dist/ folder of your checkout, so keep the checkout in place, and run make install again after pulling changes.

To remove it: make uninstall.

docs.title: With the USD nodes of Nyx
docs.text:
To run the operations of the USD nodes of Nyx (nyx-usd) in Maya, put the usd extra in the module too:

make install DIST_EXTRAS=usd

This adds sowwic-nyx-usd (the nyx_usd package) to python/. To make it the default for your checkout, put DIST_EXTRAS = usd in the Makefile before the include. The extra of the package itself is pip install "nyx-bridge-maya[usd]".

In a headless Maya (mayapy), Maya 2026 does not find its USD by itself: set the environment variable MULTI_USD_VERSION to one of the USD builds installed with Maya, such as 0.25.5 (on macOS they are the USD_<version> folders in /Applications/Autodesk/mayausd/maya2026/<release>/mayausd/). Without it import pxr fails with No module named 'pxr'. With it, pxr imports without loading any plug-in. Don't leave a standalone USD on PYTHONPATH in that process, it would be found before the one of Maya. See Starting Maya from a stage. Connect Maya as below, then select it in Nyx with client_kind = maya on the Remote Client node.

docs.title: 3. Check it in Maya
docs.text:
Restart Maya, then in the Script Editor:

import maya.cmds as cmds

cmds.loadPlugin("nyx_bridge_maya_plugin")
import nyx_bridge_maya
print(nyx_bridge_maya.__version__)

To load the plug-in on every start, tick Auto Load for nyx_bridge_maya_plugin.py in Windows > Settings/Preferences > Plug-in Manager.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text: Symptom Check Plug-in, "nyx_bridge_maya_plugin", was not found The .mod file is not in a folder of MAYA_MODULE_PATH as Maya sees it. cmds.moduleInfo(listModules=True) should list nyx_bridge_maya. No module named nyx_bridge_maya The module is found but python/ is empty: run make dist and look for errors. make install says Set MAYA_MODULE_PATH in ... The env file is missing or does not define it. The .mod points at a folder that no longer exists Run make install again from the current checkout.

docs.title: Starting Maya from a stage
docs.text:
A stage can start a headless Maya itself, wait for it to connect and run its Remote Actions in it. Use a Launch Process node around a Remote Client:

Launch Process  ->  Remote Client  ->  Remote Action ...

Settings of the Launch Process node:

Input Value command "$MAYAPY" -c "import maya.standalone; maya.standalone.initialize(name='python'); import nyx_bridge_maya; nyx_bridge_maya.serve_standalone(); maya.standalone.uninitialize()" env {"MAYAPY": "/Applications/Autodesk/maya2026/Maya.app/Contents/bin/mayapy", "MAYA_MODULE_PATH": "<folder with the nyx_bridge_maya.mod>"} timeout Seconds to wait for Maya to boot (default 60).

Nyx gives the process the address and token of its bridge server and the name it is to connect as (NYX_BRIDGE_ADDRESS, NYX_BRIDGE_TOKEN, NYX_BRIDGE_CLIENT_NAME), which serve_standalone uses. The Remote Client inside the node uses that Maya and no other.

  • MAYA_MODULE_PATH is only needed when Maya does not find the module itself. make install puts the .mod file in the folder from your .env.
  • mayapy has no event loop, so requests run on the calling thread and serve_standalone does not reconnect: it returns when Nyx asks Maya to shut down or the connection ends.
  • When the nodes inside are done Nyx asks Maya to shut down, and stops the process if it does not. The Nyx window waits while Maya boots.

docs.title: Using USD in a headless Maya
docs.text:
To run the nyx-usd nodes in this Maya, install the usd extra (make install DIST_EXTRAS=usd) and add the version of USD Maya should use to the env input:

{
  "MAYAPY": "/Applications/Autodesk/maya2026/Maya.app/Contents/bin/mayapy",
  "MULTI_USD_VERSION": "0.25.5"
}

Without MULTI_USD_VERSION a USD node fails with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pxr': mayapy can't find the USD that comes with Maya. The versions installed are the USD_<version> folders next to the mayausd.mod file Maya uses (/Users/Shared/Autodesk/modules/maya/2026/ on macOS). If you start Maya from a script, unset PYTHONPATH in it when your shell has a standalone USD there, and export MULTI_USD_VERSION instead.

docs.title: Without Nyx starting it
docs.text:
In your own mayapy script:

import maya.standalone

maya.standalone.initialize(name="python")

from nyx_bridge_maya import MayaClient

MayaClient().serve_forever()        # blocks; address from the environment or address file

serve_standalone(name, address, token, connect_timeout) takes the same settings. Give connect_timeout (seconds) to fail with ConnectionError instead of waiting forever.
